subtitle: Deepfaked Executives, Wires & Public Trust

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday, September 14, 2027, Greenville, South Carolina. The exercise starts at 09:30 Eastern. CFO Marcus Delacroix-Hume boarded a flight to Querétaro at 09:10 (lands 12:50 Eastern, no Wi-Fi); CEO Beatrix Aldgate-Moreno is in the building. At 09:40 Treasury Analyst Ines Okonkwo-Hart gets a calendar invitation from an external address to an urgent confidential meeting 'to finish the Querétaro machining acquisition'. At 10:05 she joins a video meeting in which a video of the CFO and of General Counsel Priscilla Aranguren (both synthetic, with cloned voices) instruct her to wire an 'escrow deposit' and to keep it confidential until the announcement; the details match the real, secret acquisition talks known to seven people. Four wires are requested: $480,000 at 10:50, $1,150,000 at 11:35, $620,000 at 13:10 (before the international 15:00 Eastern cutoff) and $390,000 at 15:00, to accounts at a bank abroad (an exercise bank, not real). Pressure points: callback is required by policy for new beneficiaries and payments over $250,000, but the CFO's phone is off in the air and the 'CFO' says to skip it; Treasury Manager Gareth Lindqvist-Boyd is at a plant visit; Controller Anjali Whitcombe is the second approver and is pushed by a chat message from a lookalike account; the $1,150,000 wire needs the CFO's level of approval (the 'CFO' approves on video; the Treasury Workstation's token is not his); the analyst releases the first three wires at 10:55, 11:40 and 13:15; the real CFO lands at 12:50, switches on his phone at 13:55 and calls the Controller at 14:05 asking about the payment approvals, which is the detection; the fourth wire is stopped before release (HOLD); the CISO Rafael Oyelaran-Pierce declares the incident at 14:12; evidence preservation of the recording, invitation, chat and Workstation audit log; the meeting-platform logs show the 'CFO' joined as an external guest from an outside address; SynthCheck returns a score of 0.71 with its 6 percent false positive and 11 percent false negative rates and there are no Content Credentials, so the detector is one input only; the bank fraud desk is called at 14:20 (recall, freeze, written recall within 30 minutes), the beneficiary bank freezes only the third wire's funds ($620,000) while the first two have moved on; the FBI IC3 report within 72 hours and a call to the field office because the loss exceeds $1 million, asking about the Financial Fraud Kill Chain; the insurer within 24 hours; the Audit Committee chair within 24 hours because the loss exceeds $1 million; the signed reconciliation (requested $2,640,000, released $2,250,000, stopped $390,000, frozen $620,000); at 16:20 a clip of a synthetic 'CEO' announcing the acquisition and layoffs at the Spartanburg plant appears on social media and a Greenville business reporter emails a request for comment before the 17:00 deadline; the Director of Corporate Communications must verify with the CEO, issue a holding statement within 60 minutes, send a takedown request with evidence to the platform's trust and safety team and message employees before or with the external statement; counts and amounts in every message must match the Controller's signed figures; and whether the real acquisition counterparties, vendors and suppliers who may be contacted by the same fraudsters must be warned. The SimCell plays the bank fraud desk and the beneficiary bank, the FBI, the insurer and broker, outside counsel, the platform trust and safety team, the reporter, employees at the Spartanburg plant, the acquisition counterparty and the meeting platform.
constraints: Every email address of the company uses the exercise domain tamarackprecision.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real bank, company, platform or newspaper domain; account numbers are obviously fictional.

Synthetic media items are exercise material: each carries a transcript and a text description, is marked as synthetic, and no real person's likeness or name is used; a detector score is always given with its false positive and false negative rates; amounts come only from the Controller's signed reconciliation.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; the Treasury Analyst, the real and fake executives, the bank, the FBI, the insurer, the platform, reporters and employees are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Payment controls under executive pressure, verifying identity when the executive can't be reached, keeping fraud recovery and AI incident decisions separate, and public trust when a second deepfake reaches the press.
overview.threat: On Tuesday, September 14, 2027, an outside fraudster who knows details of Tamarack's secret talks to buy a machining company in Querétaro sends a calendar invitation from an external address at 09:40 Eastern. At 10:05 Treasury Analyst Ines Okonkwo-Hart joins a video meeting on the company's video meeting service. In it, synthetic videos and cloned voices of CFO Marcus Delacroix-Hume and General Counsel Priscilla Aranguren tell her to wire a confidential "escrow deposit." The CFO boarded a flight at 09:10, before STARTEX. He has no Wi-Fi and can't take a callback. The fake "CFO" tells her to skip the callback and approves on video. A chat message from a lookalike account pushes the Controller to give the second approval. Four international wires totaling $2,640,000 are requested through the Treasury Workstation. Three are released. The fourth is put on HOLD after the real CFO calls the Controller at 14:05. At 16:20 a synthetic "CEO" clip announcing the acquisition and layoffs at the Spartanburg plant appears on social media.
overview.operationalImpact:
Treasury and accounts payable staff see a routine-looking Workstation queue. The meeting-platform logs show the "CFO" joined as an external guest. Wires go out at 10:55 ($480,000), 11:40 ($1,150,000, which needs executive-level approval that the CFO never gave in the Workstation with his own token) and 13:15 ($620,000, before the 15:00 Eastern international cutoff). The Treasury Manager is away at a plant visit, and the real CFO is out of reach until he turns on his phone at 13:55. After the CISO declares the incident at 14:12, staff must preserve the recording, the invitation, the chat and the Workstation audit log. SynthCheck scores the video at 0.71 (6 percent false positive rate, 11 percent false negative rate), and the video has no Content Credentials, so the detector is only one piece of evidence. At 14:20 the bank fraud desk is asked to recall and freeze the funds, with the written recall due within 30 minutes. The beneficiary bank freezes only the $620,000 from the third wire. The first two wires' funds have already moved on. Staff must work against several clocks:
- the FBI IC3 report within 72 hours, plus a call to the field office about the Financial Fraud Kill Chain
- the insurer and broker within 24 hours
- the Audit Committee chair within 24 hours because the loss is over $1 million

The Controller signs the reconciliation: $2,640,000 requested, $2,250,000 released, $390,000 stopped and $620,000 frozen. At 16:20 a Greenville business reporter emails for comment, with a 17:00 deadline. Spartanburg employees are calling, and the acquisition counterparty and suppliers may be contacted by the same fraudsters. Communications must check with the CEO, issue a holding statement within 60 minutes, send a takedown request to the platform, and message employees before or alongside the public statement. Every figure must match the Controller's signed reconciliation.

objectives.name: Payment Control Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to apply the TPC-FIN-04 Section 3 callback rule under executive pressure by holding the fourth pending international wire in the Treasury Workstation, refusing to treat the video 'CFO' or a lookalike chat message as verification, and calling the absent CFO and Treasury Manager only on directory numbers.

objectives.name: Fraud Recovery
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to get a complete written recall-and-freeze request (originating bank, amount, date, beneficiary account, reason) to the bank fraud desk within 30 minutes of the 14:20 call, and to track the FBI IC3, insurer and Audit Committee chair clocks against the Controller's signed reconciliation.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine and Evidence
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to declare and run a combined fraud and AI incident under TPC-SEC-02 Sections 2 and 3, preserving the meeting recording, external calendar invitation, chat and Workstation audit log, and presenting the SynthCheck 0.71 score with its 6 percent false positive and 11 percent false negative rates and the absent Content Credentials as one piece of evidence, not proof.

objectives.name: Public Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to issue a General Counsel-approved holding statement on the synthetic 'CEO' acquisition-and-layoffs clip before the Greenville reporter's 17:00 deadline, send a platform takedown request, and message Spartanburg employees no later than the public statement, using only figures signed by the Controller.

roles.name: Treasury Manager (Fraud and Treasury Lead)
roles.description: Owns first approval of payments, the hold and recall of released wires, the callback discipline in Treasury, and the payment reconciliation records under TPC-SEC-02 Section 3.
standingOrders: Callback First: no new beneficiary, out-of-calendar or out-of-workflow payment moves until the approver has completed a callback to the vendor master or directory number. A callback that does not reach the person counts as not completed, and the payment stays on hold.
Face Is Not Proof: a face or voice on a video call, a meeting the requester set up, or a 'confidential' instruction never replaces the Workstation approval with the person's own token.
Hold Beats Speed: if a release and a doubt arrive together, hold the wire and miss the cutoff rather than release and hope.
Bank Desk Now: phone the originating bank's fraud desk first and follow up in writing. Do not wait for the full picture before asking for a freeze.

roles.name: Controller
roles.description: Owns second approval of payments of $250,000 and above, executive approval with the CEO's delegate when the CFO is absent, and the signed reconciliation that every loss figure must match.
standingOrders: One Number: the only amounts anyone may use are the ones in your signed reconciliation. Re-sign it whenever a freeze or recall changes a figure.
Channel Check: approval requests that come by chat, email or a meeting link are fraud patterns until a callback on a directory number confirms them.
Delegate, Don't Assume: while the CFO is in the air, executive-level decisions go to you plus the CEO's delegate as TPC-FIN-04 Section 2 requires, never to someone who only claims to speak for him.

roles.name: Chief Financial Officer (Finance Executive)
roles.description: Owns executive approval of payments of $1,000,000 and above, approval of loss figures and bank steps, and the notice to the Audit Committee chair.
standingOrders: Confirm Absence: say clearly, in writing, that you gave no approval while in flight, and that no instruction in your name counts unless you entered it in the Workstation with your token.
Escalate Upward: brief the CEO and the Audit Committee chair through the corporate secretary within the 24-hour window. Do not wait for recovery results.
Truth Over Reassurance: approve only figures the Controller has signed, even if a smaller number would calm the board or the press.

roles.name: Chief Information Security Officer (Incident Commander)
roles.team: Team D: Chief Information Security Officer
roles.description: Manages the declaration and technical response of the combined fraud and AI incident, evidence preservation, the takedown decision, and liaison with the FBI field office and the meeting-platform vendor.
standingOrders: Declare at Once: under TPC-SEC-02 Section 2, a suspected deepfake that has already led to a payment is a fraud and AI incident from the moment it is reported.
Preserve Before Acting: lock down the recording, the external invitation, the lookalike chat account and the Workstation audit log before anyone deletes, forwards or 'cleans up' anything.
Score With Caveats: report SynthCheck as 0.71 with its 6 percent false positive and 11 percent false negative rates, and note that missing Content Credentials prove nothing.
Partners, Not Solo: work through the FBI field office and the platform vendor's channels for the kill chain and the takedown. Do not run your own counter-operation.

roles.name: General Counsel
roles.description: Owns legal hold, privilege, the FBI IC3 report, the insurer and broker notice, and approval of any statement that mentions a loss, fraud, an investigation or an AI system.
standingOrders: Your Voice Was Cloned: confirm on the record, internally, that you were not in the 10:05 meeting, and treat every message in your name since then as suspect.
Clock Board: track the IC3 72-hour, insurer 24-hour and Audit Committee 24-hour clocks by the hour, and do not let recovery work push them back.
Approve, Don't Delay: review statements fast. Say only 'we have reported the matter to the FBI' about law enforcement, and never confirm the acquisition talks.

roles.name: Director of Corporate Communications
roles.team: Team F: Director of Corporate Communications
roles.description: Owns the holding statement, the employee and Spartanburg messages, scripted outreach to suppliers and the counterparty, social listening, and the takedown request for the synthetic 'CEO' clip.
standingOrders: Verify Before Voice: check with the real CEO through a directory callback before calling the clip false, and never call it fake only because a detector said so.
Employees First: Spartanburg staff hear from the company no later than the public statement.
Be First, Be Right: get a holding statement approved by the General Counsel within 60 minutes and before the 17:00 reporter deadline, using only the Controller's signed figures.
Script, Not Blast: account owners warn suppliers and the counterparty using a script. Do not send a mass email that a fraudster could copy.

phases.title: The Escrow Meeting
phases.goal: Tests whether Finance and Security treat an off-pattern but convincing executive instruction as a possible incident, or let urgency, secrecy and a familiar face override the second-channel verification in TEIVES 2 and the separation of duties in TPC-FIN-04 2.
beats: (09:40) The email security gateway delivers a calendar invitation titled 'Project escrow – confidential' from an outside address to Treasury Analyst Ines Okonkwo-Hart. The meeting platform labels it as coming from outside the Tamarack tenant (TEIVES 2, TCSP 4). The inject notes that CFO Marcus Delacroix-Hume boarded at 09:10 for Querétaro with no Wi-Fi (TCSP 6), and that the Treasury Manager is away on a plant visit.

(10:05–10:20) The SimCell plays the analyst, who calls the Controller and the Treasury Manager on her desk phone after a video meeting. In it, 'CFO' and 'General Counsel Priscilla Aranguren' told her to wire a confidential Querétaro escrow deposit and to skip the callback. Provide this item as a labeled synthetic transcript and text description. Put the amounts and the fictional beneficiary account in a separate text product.

Noise item: the SOC's managed service raises a routine endpoint alert about a blocked macro on an accounts payable laptop in Spartanburg. The CISO's analysts must triage it down while Finance asks whether IT is 'seeing anything'.

(10:40) A chat message arrives from a lookalike 'Marcus Delacroix-Hume' account. It asks the Controller to give the second approval in the Treasury Workstation 'before the counterparty walks' and tells her to keep it from colleagues. This tests TEIVES 2: tell the Controller or CISO, and call back using the directory only.

(10:55) A Workstation queue note shows wire 1 of $480,000 to an international beneficiary released before the 15:00 Eastern cutoff. It is the first record that money has actually moved. Players decide whether to escalate or wait for the CFO to land.

phases.title: Four Wires Deep
phases.goal: Tests whether, as the impact grows and the real CFO can finally be reached, players stop business as usual, recognise the meeting-platform and Workstation evidence for what it shows, and get the CISO to formally declare a combined fraud and synthetic-media incident under TPC-SEC-02.
beats: Time jump: the Workstation audit log shows wire 2 of $1,150,000 released at 11:40 with an executive-level approval the CFO never entered with his own multi-factor token (TPC-FIN-04 2). Wire 3 of $620,000 was released at 13:15. Wire 4 of $390,000 is pending in the queue.

Red herring: the Poznań line reports that the supplier-quality vision model is rejecting good parts. The AI Governance Lead asks the CISO to agree a pause under TPC-SEC-02 6, which pulls Security attention and raises the provider/deployer question. Players must keep it separate from the fraud, because no Tamarack AI system was used in the scheme.

Visual confirmation for the room: a screen capture of the meeting platform's admin log shows that 'CFO' and 'General Counsel' joined as external guests from outside addresses, along with the invitation source (TCSP 4).

(13:55–14:05) The real CFO turns on his phone in Querétaro and calls the Controller: 'I approved nothing.' The Controller places wire 4 ($390,000) on HOLD in the Workstation. Players must confirm the call by calling the CFO back on his directory number, not the number shown.

(14:12) The CISO declares the incident as Incident Commander. A Spartanburg supervisor calls Communications about a rumour of an acquisition and layoffs. This is early misinformation that the Director of Corporate Communications (Dorothea Skarsgaard-Blum) must log without confirming anything.

phases.title: Recall and Freeze
phases.goal: Tests the shift from automated payment flow to manual, callback-verified operation. It covers the race to recall funds through the First Meridian fraud desk, preserving evidence, and the one high-consequence decision on suspending outgoing payments.
beats: (14:20) The First Meridian Commercial Bank fraud line (800-555-0141) takes the verbal recall and asks for a written recall-and-freeze request within 30 minutes. The request must name the originating bank, each amount, the date, the beneficiary accounts and the reason. Wire 2 is called out as needing a separate recall request.

Forensics smoking gun: the SOC preserves the recording, the external calendar invitation, the lookalike chat and the Workstation audit log. SynthCheck returns 0.71 on the 'CFO' video, with a 6 percent false positive rate and an 11 percent false negative rate, and C2PA validation finds no Content Credentials. The analyst's verification note must present this as one piece of evidence, not proof.

DECISION POINT (14:35): the CISO, Controller and CFO by phone must choose. Option one: suspend all Workstation releases to the bank and run every payment by manual directory callback. The cost is that legitimate supplier wires and Mexican peso payments miss the 15:00 international cutoff, and Thursday's roughly $3.2 million steel and tooling run is put at risk. Option two: keep releasing, accept that more compromised approvals may exist, and revoke only the Controller's and CFO's tokens.

Consequence of manual mode: Accounts Payable has a queue of supplier callbacks logged in the ERP (TCSP 3). A Querétaro counterparty contact reports a 'Tamarack' call asking to confirm escrow details. Account owners must warn the counterparty using a script, not an email blast (TEIVES 5).

(15:10) The beneficiary bank reports that it froze only the $620,000 from wire 3, and that the funds from wires 1 and 2 have already moved on. Players start the clocks: the FBI IC3 report within 72 hours plus a call to the field office about the Financial Fraud Kill Chain, the insurer and broker within 24 hours, and the Audit Committee chair within 24 hours.

phases.title: Second Deepfake, Signed Figures
phases.goal: Tests whether Tamarack can restore trust in both its payment data and its public voice. That means checking recovery claims instead of accepting them, publishing only figures the Controller has signed, and handling a second synthetic clip under TEIVES 4 and 5 before a media deadline.
beats: (16:20) A synthetic 'CEO' clip announcing the Querétaro acquisition and layoffs at the Spartanburg plant appears on a fictional social platform. It is labeled exercise material with a transcript. At the same time, a Greenville business reporter emails for comment with a 17:00 deadline. Communications must verify the clip with the CEO on site before calling it fake, and must preserve the URL, the account, the time first seen and the view count (TEIVES 4).

Restoration claim: IT reports that external guest access is now blocked on the meeting platform and that 'the Workstation is clean'. First Meridian and the insurer's broker ask for guarantees. Players must say how they know: token resets, an audit-log review of every approval since 09:40, and directory callbacks on any pending beneficiaries.

Technical hurdle: the Treasury Workstation vendor will release the full audit-log export only after a support ticket and a signed access request. This delays the evidence package for the FBI field office and the insurer.

The holding statement must go out within 60 minutes and be under 150 words. It needs General Counsel approval and the CFO's approval of any figure (TEIVES 5). It must be sent with the Spartanburg employee message going out no later than the statement, and with a takedown request logged with the platform's trust and safety team.

Tedious reconciliation leads to ENDEX. The Controller signs: $2,640,000 requested, $2,250,000 released, $390,000 stopped and $620,000 frozen. Any figure that does not match is sent back. The CISO commits to the timeline within 5 working days, and to policy updates within 30 days, under TPC-SEC-02 8.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed. Go around the room by team (Treasury, Controller, SOC/CISO, Legal, Communications) so every function speaks, and write each item on the whiteboard in two columns before you discuss any of them.

questions.text: At 10:05 a 'CFO' on video told you to skip the callback, and a lookalike chat account pushed the Controller for the second approval. The 09:40 invite (I-01) already had an external-sender banner and an 'Organizer is outside the Tamarack tenant' warning. When did each of you stop trusting what you saw and heard? Why did a face and a voice count as verification when the CFO's directory number did not? What exactly would have made you hang up and call the Treasury Manager or the CFO's office on directory numbers before the first wire went out?

At 14:35 (I-15) you had 19 approved payments in the queue, a 15:00 peso cutoff for Querétaro suppliers, and a shared release-desk token, WS-TKN-2291, with two approvals outside its role that nobody had explained. The AP Supervisor wanted a yes or no in ten minutes. What did you decide about the fourth wire and the rest of the queue, and who made the call? Did you reach the CFO on his directory mobile even though his token was in his bag? Under the TPC-FIN-04 Section 2 approval chain, which information or pre-agreed rule would have let you decide in two minutes instead of ten?

Three wires were released. Did a complete written recall-and-freeze request (originating bank, amount, date, beneficiary account, reason) reach the bank fraud desk within 30 minutes of the 14:20 call, or did it sit with someone waiting for the figures? TPC-SEC-02 Section 7 sets several deadlines: the 24-hour clock for the insurer, the FBI IC3 filing, the call to the local FBI field office because the loss tops $1 million, and the Audit Committee chair. When did you first bring in the FBI or another law-enforcement contact? Were you working from the Controller's signed reconciliation or from numbers people remembered?

The SOC exported the meeting recording at 14:16, and the external organizer deleted the original at 14:24. You came within eight minutes of losing the main evidence. When did you declare a combined fraud and AI incident under TPC-SEC-02, and when did you ask the meeting platform vendor to preserve the evidence, given that the vendor would not release server-side logs without a support ticket and a preservation request signed by Legal? When you briefed leadership on the I-14 verification note, did you present the SynthCheck score of 0.71, with its 6% false-positive and 11% false-negative rates, as proof or as one piece of evidence next to the guest-join records, the misused token and the CFO's own denial? How did you treat the absent Content Credentials?

At 14:15 (I-11b) the Spartanburg second-shift lead called Communications, needing something to tell workers before the 15:30 shift change. At 16:20 a synthetic 'CEO' clip announcing the acquisition and layoffs went public, and the Greenville reporter's deadline was 17:00. What did you tell the employees, the reporter and the platform before you could confirm anything, and did the General Counsel approve it? Did Spartanburg staff hear from you no later than the public did? What would have let you have a holding statement ready before the clip appeared, without confirming the secret Querétaro deal?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Decisions made in the room are discussed to improve Tamarack's plans and are not used to judge individual players.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players should not challenge injects or the timeline, even where today's facts at Tamarack would differ.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including TPC-FIN-04, TPC-SEC-02, TEIVES and the TCSP. Where a plan is silent or unclear, players say what they would do and note the gap for the hot wash.
Players act on the information available to them at the start of each module and the injects delivered during it. They do not assume knowledge that a later inject has not yet given them.
All beneficiaries, banks, accounts, platforms and outlets marked EXERCISE or fictional are invented. Synthetic media is described in text and is never played.
artificialities: The scenario clock jumps between modules (to 13:50, 14:18 and 16:15 Eastern) while the room clock moves in one-hour blocks. Events in the gaps are given on facilitator time-jump cards.

A Simulation Cell (SimCell) plays everyone outside the room. Injects arrive on paper or on screen. Deepfake video, audio and chat are described in text only. No real person's likeness or voice is used.

**Module 3: Recall and Freeze (14:18–15:15 Eastern; room clock 2:00–3:00)**

It is 14:18 Eastern. At 14:05 the real CFO called the Controller from Querétaro and said he approved nothing; the security duty officer has since reached him on his directory number.
